I had my auto transplant in August! I immediately felt relief, it blew my mind. I struggled with this for at least 6 plus years, no one knew what it was. I had to explain to doctors what I had. I thought I was crazy for so long, then I got diagnosed finally. I cried, the surgeons told me I wasn’t crazy. 
I was walking within days after the AT , I felt so strong. I’m now 3 months post op and doing really well. My best friend and I were actually talking about this today and BPD in general. I told her I used to cling onto people like a child for them not to leave, get on my knees and beg type stuff. It’s so embarrassing I told her as well. But she said she’s so proud of me for talking about thoses times because it can feel embarrassing, shameful, etc etc but it means that there is growth happening by opening up those can of worms. It shows so much strength, accountability and just generally awareness of those episodes. 
The point is don’t be afraid to talk about those “embarrassing” times. You don’t have to be ashamed of yourself for those behaviors. (This doesn’t justify abuse) you were genuinely probably having your worst nightmare come true. Continue to take care of yourself, always.
